analysis: The PR modifies only docs/architecture/inference.md, a documentation file. The changed ranges are the cluster onboarding stop-handling prose around head lines 453-473 and small edits in the reasoning-parser section (head lines 3239-3242 and 3255-3286). I examined the two supplied base-text units (lines 3219-4013), which cover the reasoning/tool-parser, Qwen JSON constraint, reasoning-effort and MiMo sections. The patch excerpt is truncated, so the head text of the cluster-stop section was not fully visible. No executable code, trust-boundary, authentication, encryption or authorization behavior changes in the supplied evidence. The prose describes `darkbloom cluster stop` and `stop`/`restart` ending a cluster onboarding wait, a stop counter (`ClusterSetupRecord.stopsAsked`) exposed in `ClusterControlReply`, and a recheck under the command lock. This is orientation for the next pass. The relevant threat model is TB-014/T-062 (cluster gpu-limit) and the A-018/TB-012 availability family. Whether the stop counter and leader-step wire fields (`stopsBefore`, `stopsAsked`) are authenticated between peer Macs, and whether a remote or peer Mac can trigger a stop on the leader, cannot be judged from the docs alone. If the source implementing this is in the PR, it should be reviewed for peer authentication and for stop-spoofing denial of service. The reasoning-section edits are documentation about parser selection and do not alter the threat posture of T-041 or the prefix-cache storage entries. I identified no concrete regression from the visible evidence, and the truncated patch limits my confidence.
